mainTopic: Minimum amounts for vows to the מקדש: metals, wine, oil, and an עולה
overview: Just before this passage, the גמרא taught that someone who vows 'הרי עלי למזבח' must bring לבונה, because only לבונה goes entirely onto the altar. It finishes testing that rule against the bird עולה, wine נסכים and מנחת נסכים. Next it explains the משנה's minimums for vows of metal. Gold and silver must be at least a דינר. Copper must be worth at least a silver מעה, or enough for a small hook according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. Iron must be enough for a כליה עורב. A new משנה sets the minimum for wine at three לוגין and for oil at one לוג, while רבי says three. The גמרא gives the פסוקים for wine and debates the root of the oil argument, and רב פפא gives in to a ברייתא. The amud ends with a new משנה on vowing an עולה, including cases where he forgot which animal he named, and that ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The bird offering is not fully burned either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes answering an earlier question: the bird עולה is not entirely for the altar, because its crop and feathers are not burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The crop and the feathers (of the bird עולה are not burned on the altar).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a question asked just before this passage: 'Isn't the bird עולה entirely for the altar?' Its answer: no, because the crop and feathers are removed and thrown aside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim being defended is that only לבונה goes entirely onto the altar. A bird עולה looks like a full burnt offering, but its crop and feathers are thrown next to the altar and are not burned. So it is not a true example of 'all for the altar,' and the rule about לבונה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The crop of a bird, a pouch in its throat where food collects.
Feathers.
A bird brought as a burnt offering.

steps.confusionAlert: This line is the second half of an exchange that started before this passage. The question it answers ('isn't there the bird עולה?') is not printed here.

phrases.english: The crop and feathers.
phrases.notes: This answers the question just before: 'But isn't there the bird עולה?' These parts are thrown aside, not burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the defense against the challenge from עולת העוף, which was raised just before this passage.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual detail about how the offering is done shows it is not entirely for the altar.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bird עולה seems to be completely burned, so 'למזבח' could mean a bird עולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Its crop and feathers are not burned, so only לבונה is truly entirely for the altar.

steps.title: What about wine libations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: wine נסכים seem to go entirely to the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: But aren't there wine libations, which go entirely to the altar?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another offering that seems to be completely for the altar: the wine נסכים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If wine נסכים are entirely poured onto the altar, then someone saying 'הרי עלי למזבח' might mean wine, not לבונה. That would undo the rule that he must bring לבונה.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't there...? A standard way of raising a counter-example.
Wine libations poured at the altar.

phrases.english: But aren't there wine libations,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the bird עולה is set aside, the גמרא tries a new counter-example.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only לבונה is entirely for the altar.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wine נסכים seem to be given wholly to the altar, so they would be another option.

steps.title: The wine goes down to the drainpipes
steps.stepSummary: The wine is not actually consumed on the altar; it flows down into the שיתין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wine goes down to the drainpipes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the wine does not really stay on the altar. It runs down channels into the שיתין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being 'entirely for the altar' means being consumed on the altar itself. The wine is poured into ducts and drains away below, so it does not count. The rule about לבונה still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Deep drainage pits under the altar where the libations flowed.
They go.

phrases.english: They go to the drainpipes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from wine נסכים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the counter-example does not really fit the category.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wine נסכים are wholly given on the altar.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wine drains into the שיתין, so it is not consumed on the altar.

steps.title: What about the meal offering brought with libations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again: the מנחת נסכים is fully burned on the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't there the meal offering brought with the libations, which is fully burned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more counter-example: the flour offering that comes with the wine. It is entirely burned on the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the wine, the מנחת נסכים really is burned completely on the altar. So it seems to be a real second example of 'all for the altar,' which would challenge the rule about לבונה.

keyTerms.meaning: The flour offering brought together with the wine libations; it is burned entirely.

phrases.english: But isn't there the meal offering of libations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the wine is set aside, the גמרא challenges with the flour that comes with it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only לבונה is entirely for the altar.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מנחת נסכים is truly burned completely, so it seems to be another 'all for the altar' item.

steps.title: A מנחה is not a clear example of 'all for the altar'
steps.stepSummary: Since most kinds of מנחה are partly eaten by כהנים, the word 'מנחה' does not clearly mean 'all for the altar,' so the vow does not point to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since there are kinds of מנחה that the כהנים eat from, it is not clear-cut to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the מנחת נסכים is still a type of מנחה. Since other kinds of מנחה are mostly eaten by כהנים, it is not an obvious example of 'all for the altar.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is what the vower clearly meant. 'למזבח' points to something that is always and clearly entirely for the altar. Since the category מנחה usually includes a part the כהנים eat, it is not clear-cut, and only לבונה fits without doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: The כהנים eat (from it).
It is not clear-cut for him; it is not a definite case.
Since; because.

steps.whatToRemember: After all the challenges, the rule stands: one who vows 'למזבח' brings לבונה, because only לבונה is clearly and always entirely for the altar.

phrases.english: Since there is a meal offering
that the priests eat from,
it is not clear-cut for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאִיכָּא מִנְחָה דְּאָכְלִי כֹּהֲנִים מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from מנחת נסכים and closes the discussion of 'הרי עלי למזבח'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Looks at the whole category to decide what the vower clearly meant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the מנחת נסכים is fully burned, 'למזבח' could mean it.
steps.terutzMaskana: מנחה as a category is not clearly 'all for the altar,' so the vower must mean לבונה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that vows are understood by what the words clearly point to, not by every possible case that might fit.

steps.title: A vow of gold: at least a gold דינר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: one who vows 'gold' must give at least a דינר זהב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says 'I take upon myself gold,' he may not give less than a gold דינר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about a person who vows to give 'gold.' It quotes the rule so it can examine it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets a minimum: a gold דינר. The steps that follow ask why the vower can't fulfill his words with something smaller.

keyTerms.meaning: I take upon myself; the standard wording of a vow to give.
He may not give less than.
A gold דינר coin.

phrases.english: 'I take upon myself gold' –
he may not give less than a gold dinar.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי עָלַי זָהָב לֹא יִפְחוֹת מִדִּינַר זָהָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the לבונה discussion is finished, and the גמרא turns to the vow of gold.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who vows 'gold' must give at least a gold דינר.

steps.title: Maybe he meant a small piece of gold
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the vow can't be fulfilled with a small lump of gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he meant a small piece of gold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה: the word 'gold' could just mean a bit of gold, not a coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a vow is satisfied with the smallest amount the words can mean. 'Gold' does not have to mean a coin, so why does the משנה demand a full gold דינר?

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps.
A piece or bar of metal, not a coin.

phrases.english: But perhaps a piece of gold?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's rule just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's minimum of a gold דינר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Gold' could mean any small piece of gold, which would be less than a דינר.

steps.title: He said 'coin'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the משנה is talking about someone who said 'a gold coin.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: It is a case where he said 'a coin.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers that the משנה's case is when the person said 'a gold coin,' not just 'gold.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: By narrowing the case, a piece of gold is ruled out, since he clearly vowed a coin. That explains why a coin is required, but not which coin. Steps 9-10 take that up.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
where he said 'coin.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about a piece of gold.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case of the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He said only 'gold,' so a small piece would be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: He said 'a gold coin,' so a coin is required.

steps.title: Maybe he meant tiny coins
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: even if he said 'coin,' maybe he meant a small coin like a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he meant small coins, like פרוטות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further: 'coin' does not have to mean a דינר. It could be a tiny coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's answer explains why a coin is needed, but not why it must be as big as a דינר. The smallest coin would seem to be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Small coins, like פרוטות.

phrases.english: But perhaps small coins?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's answer: even a coin could be smaller than a דינר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement of a full gold דינר even when he said 'coin.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The smallest coin would fulfill 'a gold coin,' so why a דינר?

steps.title: Nobody makes small coins of gold
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that small change is not made of gold, so the smallest gold coin is the דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: People do not make small coins out of gold.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that tiny coins are never made of gold. So 'a gold coin' must mean at least a gold דינר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depends on how money was actually made. Small coins were made of cheaper metals, so the smallest gold coin is the דינר, and that is the minimum the vow requires.

keyTerms.meaning: Gold (Aramaic).
People do not make (or do) this.

steps.whatToRemember: A vow of 'gold' means a gold coin, as רבי אלעזר explains, and the smallest gold coin is a דינר, since small coins are not made of gold.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
People do not make small coins of gold.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא פְּרִיטֵי דְּדַהֲבָא לָא עָבְדִי אִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about small coins and confirms the משנה's minimum.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reality: how coins are actually made.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'A gold coin' could be a tiny gold coin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Gold is not made into small coins, so the minimum is a gold דינר.

steps.title: One who vows silver gives at least a silver דינר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: one who vows 'silver' must give at least a דינר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'silver,' he must give no less than a דינר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from gold to silver and quotes the משנה's rule. This sets up the same questions it just asked about gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone vowed 'silver' to the בית המקדש without saying how much. The משנה sets the minimum at a silver דינר.

keyTerms.meaning: Silver
He may not give less than
A standard silver coin

phrases.english: "Silver": he may not give less than a dinar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the gold case (steps 6-10) to the parallel silver case in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who vows silver must give at least a silver דינר.

steps.title: Why not a small lump of silver?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he can't fulfill his vow with a small piece of silver.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe he meant a small piece of silver?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה with the same question it asked about gold. He only said 'silver,' so why must he give a whole coin?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'silver' could mean any amount of the metal, even a tiny piece. So why does the משנה require a full דינר?

keyTerms.meaning: But perhaps
A lump or bar of metal that is not a coin

phrases.english: But perhaps he meant a piece of silver?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the minimum stated in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's requirement of a full דינר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain word 'silver' could be satisfied by any small amount of the metal.

steps.title: He said 'a silver coin'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers that the משנה is talking about someone who said 'coin.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: this is where he said 'a coin.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the challenge. The משנה is talking about someone who vowed a silver coin, not just silver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he said 'coin,' a plain lump of silver does not fulfill his vow. This is the same answer רבי אלעזר gave for gold.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
This is where he said "a coin."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow was for any amount of silver.
steps.terutzMaskana: The vow specified a coin, so it must be an actual coin.

steps.title: Maybe he meant a small silver coin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: even if he said 'coin,' maybe he meant a small coin like a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he meant small coins?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back again. A coin does not have to be a דינר. Smaller coins exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the vow was for a coin, the smallest silver coin might be smaller than a דינר. So why does the משנה demand a דינר?

keyTerms.meaning: Small change, low-value coins like פרוטות

phrases.english: But perhaps he meant small coins?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אלעזר's answer from step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's answer that he said 'coin'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A 'coin' could be a small coin worth less than a דינר.

steps.title: Only where small silver coins are not used
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the משנה is talking about a place where small silver coins do not circulate.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: this is in a place where small silver coins are not in use.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers that the משנה's rule applies in a place where people do not use small silver coins. There the smallest silver coin is the דינר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With gold, the answer was simple: there are no small gold coins at all. With silver, small coins do exist in some places, so the rule is limited to places where they are not used.

keyTerms.meaning: A place
Circulate, are in use
Silver (Aramaic)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the silver answer is the same as the gold one. For gold, small coins never exist. For silver, they do in some places, so the rule depends on local currency.
steps.whatToRemember: A vow of a 'silver coin' means the smallest silver coin in use, which is a דינר only where small silver coins are not used.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshes said:
In a place where they do not circulate
small coins of silver.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: בְּאַתְרָא דְּלָא סָגוּ פְּרִיטֵי דְכַסְפָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14 and closes the silver discussion.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific location
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A small silver coin could fulfill the vow.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where small silver coins are not used, the smallest silver coin is a דינר.

steps.title: One who vows copper gives at least a silver מעה's worth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: one who vows 'copper' must give at least the value of a silver מעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'copper,' he must give no less than the value of a silver מעה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next case in the משנה, copper. This sets up a different opinion on the copper minimum.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Copper is cheaper than silver, so the משנה measures it by value. He must give copper worth at least one silver מעה, a small coin.

keyTerms.meaning: Copper
A small silver coin, worth a sixth of a דינר

phrases.english: "Copper": he may not give less than the value of a silver ma'ah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from silver to the משנה's copper case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who vows copper must give copper worth at least a silver מעה.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: enough for a small copper hook
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who says the minimum is enough copper to make a small hook.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says he may not give less than a small copper hook.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a different measure for copper. Instead of a money value, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב sets the minimum by a useful object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה measures copper by its value. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב measures it by the smallest useful copper item: a small hook.

keyTerms.meaning: A hook or small pointed tool
Small

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר –
phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִפְחוֹת מִצִּינּוֹרָא קְטַנָּה שֶׁל נְחֹשֶׁת.
phrases.english: He may not give less than a small copper hook.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different measure for the copper vow in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The copper minimum is enough to make a small copper hook.

steps.title: What is the hook used for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a small copper hook is good for in the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it useful for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. If the hook is the minimum, it must have some real use in the בית המקדש, so what is it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A donation should be something usable. The גמרא wants to know what job this tiny hook does.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it fit for?

phrases.english: For what is it suitable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the hook mentioned in step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The use of a small copper hook in the בית המקדש.

steps.title: Used to clean the wicks and lamps of the מנורה
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the hook is used to scrape out wicks and clean the lamps.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: they use it to scrape out wicks and to clean the lamps.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers that the hook is a cleaning tool for the מנורה. It scrapes out old wicks and cleans the lamps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows the hook has a real use in the בית המקדש. That is why it can be the minimum copper donation.

keyTerms.meaning: Scrape out, dig out
Wicks
Wipe clean
Lamps

phrases.english: Abaye said:
That they scrape out wicks with it,
and they clean lamps with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hook is used to scrape wicks and clean the lamps of the מנורה.

steps.title: Iron: at least enough for a raven-repelling spike
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes אחרים: one who vows iron must give at least enough for a כליה עורב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Iron: a ברייתא teaches that אחרים say he may not give less than a raven-repelling spike.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a case the משנה left out, iron. A ברייתא sets the minimum as enough iron for a כליה עורב, a spike that keeps ravens off the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the copper hook, the iron minimum is measured by a useful item. The כליה עורב kept birds from landing and dirtying the holy area.

keyTerms.meaning: Iron
Literally 'raven-destroyer,' iron spikes that keep ravens away

phrases.english: Iron: it is taught in a baraita that others say:
He may not give less than a raven-repelling spike.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the list of metals beyond the משנה to iron.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who vows iron must give at least enough for a כליה עורב.

steps.title: How big is it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much iron a כליה עורב needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the actual size, so we know exactly how much iron must be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming an object is not enough for a vow. We need a clear measurement.

keyTerms.meaning: And how much?

phrases.english: And how much is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the size of the item in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size of a כליה עורב.

steps.title: A cubit by a cubit
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers: one אמה by one אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: a cubit by a cubit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives the size: a square plate one אמה by one אמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the vow has a clear minimum. He must give enough iron for a square one אמה on each side.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, about 18-24 inches
A square, one cubit by one cubit

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
A cubit by a cubit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: אַמָּה עַל אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A כליה עורב is one אמה by one אמה.

steps.title: Another version: the ברייתא itself says a cubit by a cubit
steps.stepSummary: Some say the ברייתא's wording is: he may not give less than an אמה by an אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: he may not give less than a cubit by a cubit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the same ברייתא. Here the ברייתא itself gives the measurement, and that sets up a question about its use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the ברייתא named the item and רב יוסף gave the size. In this version, the ברייתא gives the size, and the question becomes what it is for.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
He may not give less than a cubit by a cubit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: לֹא יִפְחוֹת מֵאַמָּה עַל אַמָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the iron ברייתא from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who vows iron must give at least one אמה by one אמה.

steps.title: What is a cubit-square of iron used for?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what an אמה by אמה piece of iron is good for.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what is it suitable?
steps.whatsHappening: In this version, the גמרא asks what use this size of iron has in the בית המקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The size is now known, but a donation should have a real purpose. The question is what that purpose is.

phrases.english: For what is it suitable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the measurement given in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The use of an אמה by אמה piece of iron.

steps.title: For a raven-repelling spike
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that it is used for a כליה עורב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: for a raven-repelling spike.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers that this size of iron is used to make a כליה עורב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree on the result: a כליה עורב that is one אמה by one אמה. They only differ in which part the ברייתא said and which part רב יוסף explained.
steps.whatToRemember: For iron, both versions end the same way: the minimum is enough for a כליה עורב, which measures one אמה by one אמה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
For a raven-repelling spike.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24 and closes the second version.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An אמה by אמה piece of iron is used for a כליה עורב.

steps.title: The minimum amounts for a pledge of wine or oil
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who pledges wine must bring at least three לוגין. Someone who pledges oil must bring at least one לוג, but רבי says three לוגין.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone says "I take upon myself to bring wine," he may not bring less than three לוגין. If he says "oil," he may not bring less than one לוג. רבי says: three לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets the smallest amount of wine or oil a person must bring when he pledges it without naming an amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine is fixed at three לוגין, the smallest amount of wine poured with any animal (a lamb). For oil there is a מחלוקת. The תנא קמא says one לוג, the oil used in the smallest מנחה. רבי says three לוגין, the oil in the מנחה brought with a lamb.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is upon me": the wording of a pledge, which makes the person responsible to bring it
A measure for liquids (plural: לוּגִּין)
He may not bring less than...
The basic teaching that the גמרא discusses (here written מַתְנִי׳)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי's three לוגין is about oil only. Everyone agrees that wine is three לוגין. The מחלוקת is just whether oil needs one לוג or three.

phrases.english: MISHNA: "It is upon me [to bring] wine"
he may not bring less than three log;
[if he said] "oil," he may not bring less than a log.
Rabbi says: three log.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ ״הֲרֵי עָלַי יַיִן״ – לֹא יִפְחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה לוּגִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of the כליה עורב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pledge of wine needs at least three לוגין. A pledge of oil needs at least one לוג according to the תנא קמא, or three לוגין according to רבי.

steps.title: He named an amount but forgot it
steps.stepSummary: If someone named the amount he pledged but cannot remember it, he must bring as much as is offered on the day with the most.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says, "I named an amount, but I do not know what I named," he must bring the amount of the day with the most.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה deals with a person who named a specific amount and then forgot it. To be safe, he brings the largest amount that is ever offered in one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he does not know how much he promised, any smaller amount might fall short of his pledge. Bringing the largest daily amount makes sure his pledge is fully covered.

keyTerms.meaning: "I specified": I named an exact amount
The day on which the most is offered
He must bring

steps.whatToRemember: When a pledge is unclear, he must bring enough to be sure he covered what he promised.

phrases.english: "I specified, but I do not know what I specified"
he must bring [an amount] like the day with the most.
phrases.notes: He means the day in the בית המקדש when the largest amount is offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״פֵּירַשְׁתִּי, וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מָה פֵּירַשְׁתִּי״ – יָבִיא כְּיוֹם מְרוּבֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the case of a pledge whose amount was forgotten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who forgot the amount he named must bring the amount of the day on which the most is offered.

steps.title: A פסוק teaches that wine may be pledged on its own
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word "אזרח" that a person may pledge wine by itself, and that the amount is three לוגין.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The רבנן taught: "אזרח" (native born) teaches that one may pledge wine. And how much? Three לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It brings a ברייתא that shows the source in the תורה for the משנה's rule about pledging wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally wine is poured together with a קרבן. The word "אזרח" teaches that a person may also pledge wine by itself. The ברייתא gives the amount as three לוגין, the same as the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה (here written גְּמָ׳)
"Native born": a word in the פסוק about נסכים
They may pledge as a voluntary gift (נדבה)
It teaches

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
"Native born" teaches that one may pledge wine,
and how much? Three log.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind the משנה's rule about pledging wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine may be pledged on its own, and the amount is three לוגין.

steps.title: Where do we learn that he may bring more?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for the source that a person may bring more than three לוגין if he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that if he wants to add, he may add?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a question. It is setting up the next step, which will give a פסוק as the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three לוגין has been set as the amount. Now the ברייתא asks whether that is a fixed amount or only a minimum, so that he may bring more.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?
He wants
To add more

phrases.english: And from where [do we know] that if he wants to add, he may add?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the three לוגין just mentioned may be increased.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that a person may pledge more than three לוגין of wine.

steps.title: The word "יהיה" allows bringing more
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the word "יהיה" in the פסוק teaches that he may add.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "shall be."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from step 29. The word "יהיה" is the source that he may bring more wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the wine of ראש חודש could have been written without the word "יהיה." Because the word is extra, the ברייתא learns from it that other, larger amounts of wine may also be brought.

keyTerms.meaning: "The פסוק teaches": introduces the source in the תורה
"Shall be": the word used here to allow bringing more

phrases.english: The verse states: "shall be."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word "יהיה" teaches that a person may bring more than three לוגין.

steps.title: Maybe he may bring less?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests that perhaps a person may also bring less than three לוגין.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might have thought he may bring less?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: since he may add, maybe he may also go below three לוגין. This sets up the next step, which rules it out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we learned that the amount can go up, one might think the amount is flexible in both directions. The ברייתא raises this idea so that it can reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: "One might have thought": introduces an idea that will be rejected
He may bring less

phrases.english: One might have thought he may bring less?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since adding is allowed, the ברייתא asks whether bringing less is also allowed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person may bring less than three לוגין of wine.

steps.title: The word "ככה" forbids bringing less
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the word "ככה" teaches that he may not bring less than three לוגין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: "in this manner."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the idea from step 31. The word "ככה" shows that three לוגין is the least he may bring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "ככה" means "this way," so the תורה is setting a fixed minimum. Together with "יהיה," the rule is that he may bring more than three לוגין but never less.

keyTerms.meaning: "In this manner": the word showing he may not go below the set amount
A set amount required by halacha

steps.whatToRemember: Wine may be pledged on its own ("אזרח"). The amount is at least three לוגין: he may bring more ("יהיה") but never less ("ככה").

phrases.english: The verse states: "in this manner."
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:13, the same פסוק as "אזרח" earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea in step 31 and finishes the ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word "ככה" teaches that he may not bring less than three לוגין.

steps.title: The משנה's rule for pledging oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line of the משנה about oil. The רבנן say the minimum is one לוג, and רבי says three לוגין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone pledges oil, he may not bring less than one לוג. רבי says: three לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes its rule about pledging oil by itself. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just before this, we learned that wine pledged by itself must be at least three לוגין. Now we see a disagreement about oil. The unnamed first opinion says one לוג is enough. רבי says three, the same amount as wine.

keyTerms.meaning: Oil, here meaning oil donated to the מקדש by itself
A measure of liquid volume
He may not bring less than

phrases.english: Oil: he may not bring less than a log,
Rabbi says: three log.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wine discussion (steps 28-32) to the next case in the משנה, oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Oil pledged by itself has a minimum of one לוג according to the רבנן and three לוגין according to רבי.

steps.title: What are they arguing about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle lies behind the disagreement between the רבנן and רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind each side. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on either opinion. The גמרא wants to find the underlying idea that makes one side say one לוג and the other side say three.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (What is the root of the argument?)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the disagreement just quoted from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides the רבנן and רבי about the minimum amount of oil.

steps.title: Two ways of learning one case from another
steps.stepSummary: The Sages tell רב פפא that the argument is about how far a comparison reaches. One side copies the source case completely. The other side borrows only one point and takes the rest from the case's own category.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages said before רב פפא: they disagree about 'learn from it, and again from it' versus 'learn from it, but set it in its own place.'
steps.whatsHappening: The answer names two different ways of comparing cases. The גמרא says the רבנן and רבי each follow a different one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'דון מינה ומינה,' once you learn one rule from a source case, you take all its details too. With 'דון מינה ואוקי באתרה,' you learn only the one rule, and the other details come from the place where the new case naturally belongs. The next two steps show which side holds which method.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, and again from it: copy the source case in every detail
Learn from it, but set it in its own place: borrow only one rule, and take the other details from the case's own category

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that oil is learned from מנחה. The argument is only about whether the details, such as the amount, also come from מנחה.
steps.whyThisMatters: These two methods are general tools that appear in other places in the גמרא, not only here.

phrases.english: The Sages said it before Rav Pappa:
About 'learn from it, and from it,'
phrases.notes: In other words: once you compare to a source case, copy all of its details.

phrases.english: or 'learn from it, but set it in its place':
phrases.notes: In other words: take just one point from the source, and the rest comes from where the case really belongs.

phrases.english: this is what they disagree about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 34 by naming the principle the two sides argue about.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The dispute is over 'דון מינה ומינה' versus 'דון מינה ואוקי באתרה.'

steps.title: The רבנן copy the מנחה completely
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn from מנחה that oil can be donated. They also copy the מנחה's amount of oil, so the minimum is one לוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold 'learn from it, and again from it.' Just as a מנחה can be donated, oil can be donated too. And again from it: just as a מנחה uses a לוג of oil, oil by itself is also a לוג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the רבנן's opinion using the first method.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן make two moves from the same source. First, the fact that oil can be donated comes from מנחה. Second, the amount, one לוג, also comes from מנחה. That is why their minimum is one לוג.

keyTerms.meaning: A flour offering, which comes with oil
People may donate it as a voluntary gift
So too, also

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold: learn from it, and from it.
Just as a meal offering may be donated,
so too oil may also be donated.
And from it again: just as a meal offering is with a log of oil,
so too oil by itself is a log.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the first method from step 35 to the רבנן's opinion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן copy the מנחה both for allowing a donation and for the amount, so the minimum is one לוג.

steps.title: רבי borrows one point and then compares oil to נסכים
steps.stepSummary: רבי learns from מנחה only that oil can be donated. For the amount, he puts oil back in its own category, the poured נסכים, which are three לוגין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי holds 'learn from it, but set it in its place.' Just as a מנחה can be donated, oil can be donated too. But set it in its own place, like נסכים: just as נסכים are three לוגין, oil is also three לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי's opinion using the second method. This finishes the answer to 'what are they arguing about.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי agrees with the רבנן's first move, that oil can be donated because a מנחה can. But he does not take the amount from מנחה. Oil is poured on the מזבח like נסכים, so its amount comes from נסכים, which is three לוגין.

keyTerms.meaning: Drink offerings poured on the מזבח
Three לוגין, the smallest amount for נסכים

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides learn from מנחה that oil can be donated. The רבנן also copy the מנחה's amount (one לוג). רבי takes the amount from נסכים instead (three לוגין).

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי סָבַר: דּוּן מִינַּהּ וְאוֹקֵי בְּאַתְרַהּ,
phrases.english: And Rabbi holds: learn from it, but set it in its place.
Just as a meal offering may be donated,
so too oil may also be donated.
But set it in its place, like libations.
phrases.notes: Oil is poured on the מזבח just like the drink offerings, so that is the category it belongs to.

phrases.english: Just as libations are three log,
so too oil is also three log.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי סָבַר: דּוּן מִינַּהּ וְאוֹקֵי בְּאַתְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the dispute and finishes the explanation that began in step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי takes only the donation rule from מנחה and takes the amount from נסכים, so the minimum is three לוגין.

steps.title: רב פפא says רבי learns the oil donation from אזרח
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rejects the explanation that רבי and the רבנן argue about how far a comparison reaches. Everyone agrees that if you learn from מנחה, you copy it fully. So רבי must learn the oil donation from אזרח, which is in the נסכים passage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to them: If רבי learned it from מנחה, then everyone agrees that you learn everything from that source. Rather, רבי learns it from the word 'native born.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא rejects the explanation given in Steps 35-37. He offers a different source for רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב פפא, nobody thinks a comparison to מנחה would borrow only part of the law. If רבי had learned from מנחה, he would also say one לוג, like the רבנן. Because רבי says three לוגין, his source must be the verse of אזרח in the נסכים passage, and נסכים are three לוגין.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, and again from it: copy every detail from the source case
Native born; the word in the verse about נסכים that רבי learns from
He learns it, he derives it

steps.confusionAlert: רב פפא is not adding a third opinion. He is saying the reason given in Steps 35-37 is wrong: the real argument is about which verse each side learns from.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to them:
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the Sages who gave the explanation in Steps 35-37.

phrases.english: If Rabbi learned it from the meal offering,
then everyone agrees, without dispute,
that you learn from it and again from it,
phrases.notes: In other words, everyone would copy the מנחה's amount of one לוג as well.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi learns it from 'native born.'
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:13, which is in the passage about נסכים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַב פָּפָּא: אִי מִמִּנְחָה גָּמַר לַהּ רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation of Steps 35-37 and replaces it with a different source for רבי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רבי learns from מנחה but takes only one point from it.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Everyone holds דון מינה ומינה, so a comparison to מנחה would bring the one-לוג amount along with it.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי learning from the word קרבן
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן challenges רב פפא with a ברייתא. It learns the oil donation from the word קרבן in the מנחה passage, yet it gives the amount as three לוגין, which is רבי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב נתן said to רב פפא: How can you say this? A ברייתא teaches that the word 'offering' shows one may donate oil, and the amount is three לוגין. Who says three לוגין? רבי. And he learns it from 'offering.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא is challenged with a ברייתא that seems to contradict him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word קרבן comes from the מנחה verse. The ברייתא gives the amount as three לוגין, and only רבי holds that view. So רבי does learn from מנחה, against רב פפא's claim that he learns from אזרח.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really say this? A phrase that opens a challenge
Offering; the word in the מנחה verse that teaches about donating oil
They may donate, as a voluntary gift

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Natan said to Rav Pappa:
And can you really say that?
But isn't it taught: 'Offering'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:1, the verse about a מנחה.

phrases.english: teaches that one may donate oil,
And how much? Three log.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאָמַר שְׁלֹשֶׁת לוּגִּין?
phrases.english: Whom have you heard say three log?
Rabbi, and yet he brings it from 'offering.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's claim from Step 38.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that רבי learns the oil donation from אזרח and not from מנחה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא that holds three לוגין, which is רבי's view, takes its source from קרבן in the מנחה verse.

steps.title: רב פפא accepts the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers: if that is what the ברייתא teaches, then so it is. He does not argue with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If it is taught, it is taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא admits that he cannot answer the ברייתא and accepts it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא made his claim from reasoning. A ברייתא is a stronger source, so he gives in to it. This brings the גמרא back to the view that רבי learns from מנחה, even though he says three לוגין.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is taught, it is taught: I accept the ברייתא and have no answer

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, a ברייתא shows that רבי learns the oil donation from מנחה (the word קרבן) and still holds three לוגין. רב פפא's alternative is set aside.

phrases.english: He said to him:
If it is taught, it is taught.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 39 by giving in to it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא stands: רבי learns from קרבן in the מנחה passage, and רב פפא's אזרח suggestion is dropped.

steps.title: He forgot how much oil he pledged
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: someone specified an amount of oil but forgot what it was. He must bring as much as is offered on the biggest day.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I specified, but I do not know what I specified': he brings an amount like the biggest day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up a clarification in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not know how many לוגין he pledged, so he must bring the highest amount ever offered on one day. That way his pledge is surely covered. The next step defines 'biggest day.'

keyTerms.meaning: I specified, I spelled out the amount
The biggest day, the day with the most offerings

phrases.english: 'I specified, but I do not know what I specified':
phrases.notes: This is a line from the משנה. He means he named a number of לוגין of oil and then forgot it.

phrases.english: he must bring like the greatest day.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה about pledging oil.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who forgot how much oil he pledged brings the amount offered on the day with the most offerings.

steps.title: Which day is the biggest day
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that the biggest day is the first day of סוכות when it falls on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: like the first יום טוב of the festival when it falls on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא defines what the משנה meant by 'the biggest day.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the first day of סוכות, many מוסף offerings are brought. When that day falls on שבת, the שבת מוסף is added too. So that day has the most oil of any day, and he brings that amount.

keyTerms.meaning: The festival; here it means סוכות

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The biggest day is the first day of סוכות when it falls on שבת, because the מוסף offerings of both days are brought.

steps.title: New משנה: pledging an עולה without saying which animal
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה begins. Someone who says 'I take upon myself an עולה' brings a lamb. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says a turtledove or a young pigeon is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: 'I take upon myself an עולה': he brings a lamb. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: either a turtledove or a young pigeon.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It deals with someone who pledged an עולה without saying what kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion says a plain 'עולה' means at least an animal, so he brings a lamb. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says a bird is also called an עולה, so a turtledove or young pigeon fulfills the pledge.

keyTerms.meaning: I take upon myself a burnt offering: the wording of the pledge

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new subject: an unspecified pledge of an עולה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first opinion says an unspecified עולה pledge requires a lamb; רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says a turtledove or young pigeon is enough.

steps.title: Forgot which cattle he specified
steps.stepSummary: If he said he specified an animal from the cattle but forgot which one, he brings both a פר and an עגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'I specified that my עולה would be from the cattle, but I do not know what I specified,' he must bring a bull and a calf.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its cases of an עולה vow. Now the person remembers he picked cattle, but forgot whether it was an older animal or a young one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה from cattle can be a grown bull (פר) or a young calf (עגל). Since he cannot remember which one he promised, he brings both. That way, whichever one he really said, his vow is covered.

keyTerms.meaning: Cattle, the herd animals
A grown bull
A young calf

steps.title: Forgot which animal he specified
steps.stepSummary: If he said he specified from the animals in general but forgot which, he brings all six kinds of male animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'I specified from the animals, but I do not know what I specified,' he must bring a bull and a calf, a ram, a large goat, a young goat, and a lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the person only remembers that he chose a בהמה, a farm animal, but not which kind. So he must bring every possible kind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is wider than the one before, so the list of animals gets longer. From cattle he brings a bull and a calf, from sheep a ram and a lamb, and from goats a big goat and a young goat. Bringing all six makes sure he covers whatever he actually promised.

keyTerms.meaning: A farm animal (cattle, sheep, or goats)
A grown ram
A grown male goat
A young goat
A young lamb

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think he brings only one animal and picks at random. He must bring all six, because any one of them might be what he promised.

steps.title: Forgot even the general kind he specified
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens a third case: he specified something but forgot it entirely. The ruling comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, 'I specified, but I do not know what I specified,'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The משנה starts the widest case, where he does not even remember the general type, and the ruling comes in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case so far has been wider than the one before: first cattle, then all farm animals. Now he does not remember even the category he chose, so we should expect an even longer list of things to bring.
